chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Hasan al-Razi from Abu Muhammad al-Razi from Abu al-Maghra from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'I am bearing patiently the bitter behavior of this servant of mine and my family regarding the matter of Hanzal. Indeed, whoever is patient attains through his patience the rank of the fasting one who stands in prayer, and the rank of the martyr who has struck with his sword in front of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.الصَّائِمِ الْقَائِمِ: The fasting one who stands in prayer (referring to night prayer)
key_terms.الْحَنْظَلِ: Hanzal (a type of wild cucumber), used as a metaphor for extreme bitterness

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for patience with difficult people according to Imam al-Baqir?

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates that Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s.) said, “I am bearing patiently the bitter behavior of this servant and my family regarding the matter of Hanzal. One who is patient, is like one who stays up at night for prayers,  observes  fast  and  one  who  is  martyred  while fighting alongside Muhammad (s.a.w.s.).
